rfm_tuples.R: 'Our total credit trading volume has increased from approximately $2.0 trillion in 2019 to $3.1 trillion in 2023 and our estimated market share of U.S. high-grade and high-yield corporate bond volumes in 2023 was 20.4% and 17.1%, respectively.' (10-K Item 1, p. 9) — paired with management's narrative emphasizing growth ('large opportunity remaining to capture additional market share').
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify the headline 20.4% and 17.1% against the 10-K's own market-share table (Item 1, p. 13-14) showing 2022 vs 2023. Mode B — derive: if growth narrative is honest, the year-over-year delta should be flat or up, not down. Check the 'bps Change' column.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Combined U.S. HG/HY share: 20.4% (2022) -> 19.6% (2023) = -80 bps. U.S. HG: 21.3% (2022) -> 20.4% (2023) = -90 bps. U.S. HY: 17.9% (2022) -> 17.1% (2023) = -80 bps. U.S. govt bonds: 3.5% (2022) -> 2.8% (2023) = -70 bps. ONLY municipals improved: 4.5% (2022) -> 5.9% (2023) = +140 bps. So MKTX lost share in 4 of 5 disclosed product areas including its two largest. Management framing emphasizes the multi-year level (20.4% headline = high-grade level) while burying the year-over-year deceleration.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Self-disclosed in the table, but the headline framing in Item 1 cites the FY2023 high-grade share level (20.4%) rather than the prior-year comparison; readers focused on the executive summary would not realize share is contracting. The Q1 2024 10-Q (filed 2024-05-07) confirms HG share decreased to 19.3% vs 19.9% Q1'23 — second consecutive period of HG share loss. Not lying, but the narrative is engineered to obscure a multi-period market-share decline that is a primary investor concern.

rfm_tuples.R: 'The estimated final share payouts for the 2021 and 2022 [Performance Equity] awards as of December 31, 2023 decreased 34.6% compared to December 31, 2022.' (10-K Critical Accounting Estimates, line 1713) — embedded in technical accounting estimate paragraph, not in Compensation Discussion.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — derive: PSU payout ratio is management's OWN scorecard against pre-tax adjusted operating margin and U.S. credit market share targets. If payouts compressed 34.6% in one year, management's internal forecast of its own performance has materially deteriorated against board-set targets.
rfm_tuples.M_value: PSU expected payout ratio: -34.6% YoY. Metrics underlying the 2022/2023 awards = pre-tax adjusted operating margin + U.S. credit market share + revenue growth ex-U.S. credit. The two anchor metrics are exactly the ones in MD&A trending negative. This is a quiet self-confession: the comp committee, with full inside data, expects executive PSU payouts to come in 34.6% lower because management is missing its own multi-year targets.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Most damning Mode-B finding. The disclosure is technically present but buried in a critical-accounting-estimate paragraph that no equity analyst would read for performance signal. The 34.6% PSU mark-down is the board's own forward view that the 2021-2023 performance cycle is materially missing targets. This is a high-quality, board-validated leading indicator of multi-year underperformance vs internal plan.

rfm_tuples.R: 'During the second and third quarters of 2023, we experienced challenging operating conditions ... resulted in a decrease in the duration of U.S. high-grade bonds traded on our platforms, which had a negative effect on our average variable transaction fee per million ... the low levels of credit spread volatility during the second and third quarters of 2023 contributed to a decrease in ETF market maker activity, which we believe had a negative impact on our ability to increase our U.S. high-yield volumes.' (10-K MD&A Economic Factors, line 1634)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify the cause-effect chain (duration drop -> fee/million drop; vol drop -> ETF MM dropout -> HY volume drop). Mode B — derive: if the cause is truly cyclical (volatility/duration), then market share should be flat and only fees/volume should swing. If share is also down, the cause is mis-attributed and the real driver is competitive/structural.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2024 10-Q (lines 6526, 7889) repeats the SAME cyclical explanation ('strong new issuance and low levels of credit spread volatility negatively impacted our U.S. high-yield volumes and estimated market share in the first quarter of 2024'), and admits U.S. HG share also dropped to 19.3% from 19.9%. So management has now blamed cyclical factors (vol/duration/new issuance) for SHARE losses in 4 of the last 5 quarters across both HG and HY. A cyclical headwind should not durably move share. Mode-B conclusion: structural competitive pressure (Tradeweb portfolio trading, dealer ATSs, ETF MMs going direct) is being recast as a temporary macro story.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Claim evolution from 10-K to 10-Q shows the same 'cyclical' narrative being recycled while the underlying share loss persists into Q1'24. Not a lie, but a sustained mis-attribution that delays acknowledgement of structural competition — exactly the framing that gets disrupted franchises punished when management finally concedes.

rfm_tuples.R: 'On November 6, 2023, MarketAxess Holdings Inc. was informed by Christopher N. Gerosa, the Company's Chief Financial Officer, that he will resign from such position effective January 31, 2024, to accept a position with another company. Mr. Gerosa's departure was not because of any disagreement with the Company's independent auditors or the Company on any matter...' (8-K dated 2023-11-09) + 'On January 18, 2024, the Board appointed Christopher R. Concannon, Chief Executive Officer of the Company, as interim Chief Financial Officer, effective February 1, 2024.' (8-K dated 2024-01-19)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify CFO transition timing and disagreement language against 8-K Item 5.02 + 10-K certifications. Mode B — derive: if the company is healthy, why has the CFO role remained vacant from Feb 1 to the 10-K date (Feb 22) and still vacant through Q1 10-Q (May 7) — over 3 months with the CEO doubling as CFO is unusual for a $7B-market-cap operator with a clean audit.
rfm_tuples.M_source: EDGAR 8-K Item 5.02 filings (acc 0001193125-23-274514 and 0001193125-24-011252); 10-K signatures; auditor_change_tracker.query_auditor_changes(cik='0001278021', cutoff='2024-05-15') = CLEAN_AUDITOR_TENURE, n_disagreements=0, n_8k_item_401=0
rfm_tuples.M_value: CFO departure Jan 31, 2024. CEO serves as interim CFO from Feb 1; 'actively conducting a formal search process' but still no permanent CFO as of cutoff 2024-05-15 (3.5 months vacant). Interim PAO Cianciulli (age 36, Head of External Reporting, ex-PwC, ex-Virtu) is junior for the role. Auditor PwC unchanged (PCAOB ID 238), no disagreements, no Item 4.01. rfm_tuples.interpretation: Standard 'no disagreement' boilerplate is present and the auditor is unchanged — so this is not an accounting-crisis CFO departure. But the prolonged vacancy (3.5+ months with CEO doubling) at a public capital-markets company with deteriorating share metrics is itself a soft signal: either the candidate pool is reluctant, or the board wants a strategic-finance CFO (cost-out / M&A) implying acknowledgment of competitive pressure not yet in the narrative. Mode B: in a clean franchise, you have a permanent CFO ready Feb 1; the gap is an admission.

rfm_tuples.R: 'In 2023, trading volumes in our automated trading protocols rose to $303.3 billion, up 37.8% from $220.2 billion in 2022. There were 204 active client firms using our automated and algorithmic trading protocols in 2023, up 25.9% from 2022.' (10-K Technology Environment, line 1654) + 'In 2023, we introduced X-Pro' + 'recent acquisition of Pragma'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — derive: if automated/algorithmic volume is up 37.8% and X-Pro + Pragma are accelerating execution algorithms, market share in core credit should be flat-to-up. The fact that share is down 80-90 bps in HG/HY while automation is up 37.8% means automation gains are coming from existing wallet, not new wallet — i.e., MKTX is automating retreat, not capturing share.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Automated protocol volume +37.8% YoY but combined HG/HY share -80 bps YoY. The metrics are decoupled — automation is intra-client efficiency gain, not share capture. Pragma acquisition (closed 2023) adds equities/FX algos OUTSIDE MKTX's core credit market, expanding TAM definition while core TAM share is contracting.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Classic 'good headline / bad implication' disclosure pattern. The 37.8% automation growth is real but functions as a distraction from the share story. Mode B exposes that the automation success and share loss are simultaneously true — meaning automation is necessary just to defend the existing book, and competitors are taking share at the periphery (portfolio trading) where automation alone does not win.

rfm_tuples.interpretation: Liquidity claim verifies cleanly. MKTX is in drawdown for fundamental (share/fee compression) reasons, NOT distress reasons. Important calibration: the framework should not over-penalize a healthy franchise simply because the stock is down 26.6%.

rfm_tuples.R: 'We experience cybersecurity threats and incidents from time to time. However, as of the date of this report, MarketAxess has not experienced a cybersecurity threat or incident that has materially affected the Company in at least the past three years.' (10-K, line 1655)

rfm_tuples.R: 'During the year ended December 31, 2023, approximately 15.8% of our revenue and 26.1% of our expenses were denominated in currencies other than the U.S. dollar, most notably the British Pound Sterling.' (10-K, line 4162) + Pragma acquisition (2023) noted to expand into equities/FX
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — derive: if 26.1% of expenses are FX-denominated vs 15.8% of revenue, MKTX has a structural ~10pp FX cost gearing. Pragma adds further non-USD revenue but also non-USD payroll. Check whether management has hedged or is taking the exposure.

Pragma integration may shift the ratio further toward international expense — worth monitoring.

Flagging only because the expense-FX gearing means any GBP strength compresses op-margin disproportionately — a tactical risk if management's MD&A continues to attribute margin pressure to 'investment' rather than to FX.

summary: MKTX is a HEALTHY franchise in a competitive-pressure drawdown — not a distressed/lying small-cap. Forensic profile: 0 SEVERE-distress signals on balance-sheet/audit/going-concern axis. PwC unchanged Big-4, no going concern, $749.9M revolver undrawn, dividend continuing. The TWO genuine soft-negatives are (1) the board's own PSU payouts marked down 34.6% YoY based on internal market-share/margin targets — a quiet self-confession of multi-year underperformance vs plan, buried in a critical-accounting-estimate paragraph; and (2) management persistently attributing 4-5 consecutive quarters of U.S. HG and HY market-share losses to cyclical macro factors (vol/duration/new issuance) when the underlying driver is structural competition (Tradeweb portfolio trading + dealer ATSs). CFO 3.5-month vacancy is a soft signal but auditor is clean and no Item 4.01. Net read: NEUTRAL — not a SHORT-tier (no distress, no audit/cyber/going-concern signal) and not a LONG-tier (the PSU mark-down + share-loss claim evolution argue management's near-term execution narrative is over-optimistic relative to board's own internal view).
